sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Gowramma.S who met with road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 06.10.2024 at about 4-30 pm., Gowramma.S was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA- Shankarachary vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143280099/
2 04-ND-6489 as an occupant and when the said Car was reached near Vijayapura- Jaipura bridge,
BM bypass road, Ramanagara Taluk and District, at that time the driver of Bolero City Pick Up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN- 12-AL-5643 came in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road, due to that the driver of the Car dashed to Bolero vehicle, result of which Gowramma sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Gowramma was shifted to Kempanna Hospital, Bidadi, but she was succumbed to the injury on the way to hospital.
So far the petitioners have spent sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony.
3. Prior to the accident, Gowramma was hale and healthy.
She was doing tailoring work and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of Gowramma, petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. Respondent no.2/

the insurer of Bolero City Pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 has filed written statement and contended that though two vehicles were involved in the alleged accident, but the petitioner has not impleaded the driver of both the vehicles viz., Bolero city Pick up vehicle and Maruti Suzuku vehicle bearing No.KA-04-ND-6489 as party to the petition and that the driver of both the vehicles were not holding valid driving license.

The respondent no.2 further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of Maruti Suzuki car and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero City Pick up vehicle.

5. Respondent no.4/the insurer of Maruti Suzuki vehicle bearing No.KA-04-ND-6489 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the Maruti Suzuki vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and Fitness certificate and that the said Maruti Suzuki vehicle was proceeding in slow manner, by following all traffic rules and regulations, at that time the driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle drove the same in a high speed,
without following traffic rules and stopped in the middle of the road without giving any signal and caused for the accident and that after investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of Bolero City Pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643.
The respondent no.4 further contended that at the time of alleged accident petitioner was proceeding in the car without wearing seat belt in violation of Motor Vehicle Rules.
6. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 3 have remained absent.

Hence they were placed ex- parte.
7.
On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Gowramma.S succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 06.10.2024 at about 4.30 p.m., near Vijayapura, Jaipura Bridge, BM bypass road, Ramanagara Tq and District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero City pick up Shankarachary vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143280099/
3 vehicle bearing reg No.TN-12-AL-5643?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
8. The petitioner No.1 got examined himself as Pw1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10.
On the hand, the respondent no.2 and 4 have examined their officials as R.W.1 and RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

9. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and 4 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
10.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - Partly in the Affirmative, ssue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.
3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1

: Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident i.e Gowramma.S (hereinafter called deceased) was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ND-6489 as an occupant and when the said Car was reached near Vijayapura- Jaipura bridge, BM bypass road, Ramanagara Taluk and District, at that time the driver of the Bolero City Pick Up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road, due to that the driver of the Car dashed to Bolero vehicle, result of which Gowramma sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Gowramma was shifted to Kempanna Hospital, Bidadi, but she was succumbed to the injures on the way to hospital.

12. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Inquest mahazar, spot mahazar,
sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet etc.,
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the husband of deceased by name Shankarachari, case has been registered against the driver of Bolero pickup goods vehicle in Crime No.0207/2024 of Ramanagara Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 106,125(a) and 281 of BNS 2023.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver for the offences punishable under Section 281,125(a),125(b) and 106(1) of BNS of 2023.
14.

It is true that based on the complaint lodged by the complainant against the driver of the offending vehicle, FIR was registered against him and after investigation charge sheet was filed against him.

The PW.1 during his cross examination by the learned counsel for respondent no.4 has Shankarachary vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143280099/
4 deposed that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle who without giving any signal suddenly stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road and their vehicle was proceeding slowly and that they are not claiming compensation from the insurer and insured of the car bearing No.KA-04- MD-6489.
15.

Even though PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that he is not claiming compensation from the respondent no.3 and 4 and that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and even though complaint was lodged and charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle but if the claim petition filed by the petitioners is perused,
wherein they have stated that accident in question was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of both the vehicles and that respondents no.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
16. If the averments of the complaint, charge sheet and the claim petition is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was proceeding ahead of Maruthi Car.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 60 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the left side of the road.
It is one way road.
There is divider in between two roads leading from Bangalore to Mysore and Mysore to Bangalore.

When the width of the road is sufficiently wide to an extent of 60 feet and when accident in question has occurred on the left side of the road., there was sufficient road on the right side of the said road.

Hence, when offending vehicle was proceeding on the left side of the road, the driver of the Maruthi car which was proceeding behind the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle on the right side of the road.

Further if the driver of the Maruthi car had maintained minimum distance between the two vehicles, even if the driver of the offending vehicle had suddenly stopped the vehicle without giving any signal, the driver of the Maruthi car could have avoided the accident.

Even though from the police records more particularly the complaint, spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report discloses the rash and negligent act contributed even by the driver of the Maruthi car but the investigating officer for the reason best known to him has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle.

It appears that it is because all the inmates of the Car have sustained injuries and one of the injured succumbed to the injuries, out of humanitarian ground to help the injured and family of the deceased the investigating officer might have filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle.
17. The officials of respondent no.2 and 4 company have adduced their evidence as RW.1 and RW.2 and given evidence blaming the driver of their opposite vehicle as the sole cause for the accident.
18. The Learned counsel for respondent no.4 has relied upon the judgment reported in ILR 2016 KAR 55 between M/s ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd., Vs. Smt. Bharthi Reddy & Ors.,

entities.text: ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd., Vs. Smt. Bharthi Reddy & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Tribunal has observed by relying upon the spot sketch that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Hon'ble High Court held that "the Tribunal is justified in fastening liability on the Insurer and directed to indemnify the award.
The Hon'ble High Court further held that the charge sheet filed by the jurisdictional police is the conclusive proof and that same has not been questioned or challenged by the insurer.

5 19.

sentences.text: Coming to the case in hand, on perusal of the entire police records, it can be said that the driver of both the vehicles have equally contributed negligence.

Merely because the investigating officer has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle, the court cannot by relying upon the same hold that the driver of the offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions time and again has observed that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof and the Tribunal has to independently decide the case based on the evidence placed on record.

In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.4, it was proved from the spot sketch that the accident in question was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it was observed so.
But in the present case from the spot mahazar and from the IMV report it can be gathered that negligence was contributed by the driver of both the vehicles.
As per the spot sketch, after the accident Maruthi Suzuki Car has hit to the Iron fencing.
Further as per the IMV report much damage was caused to the Car.
From the aforesaid materials also it can be gathered the speed at which Maruthi Car was at the time of accident.

Hence,
considering the materials placed on record this court is of the opinion that the driver of the both vehicles have contributed negligence at the ratio of 50:50.
Hence, point no.1 is answered in Partly affirmative.
20. Issue no 2:
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 54 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhar card of the deceased which reflects the year of birth of deceased as 1968 as per Ex.P10.
Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 56 years.

21. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing tailoring work and earning sum of Rs.20,000/-.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner no.2 is the married daughter and petitioner no.3 is the major son of the deceased.

As per the own evidence of PW.1, he is retired KEB employee and getting pension of Rs.25,000/- per month and the petitioner no.2 is the married daughter and residing in her matrimonial home and petitioner no.3 is the major son.
Hence, the petitioners being the husband, married daughter and major son of the deceased are not the dependents of the deceased though they are the legal heirs of the deceased.

23. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the ruling reported in 2004 (5) Kar. L.J 321 Division Bench between A Manavalgan Vs. A.Krishnamurthy & Ors, Wherein it was held that "the question of awarding compensation under the head "loss of dependency" would not arise in the absence of financial dependency of the claimant on income of deceased.
Claim petition to be treated as one on behalf of estate of deceased and compensation received by claimant forms part of that estate".

Shankarachary vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143280099/
6 24.

sentences.text: In ILR 2008 KAR 1561 between M/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shivamma & Ors.

entities.text: ILR 2008 KAR 1561 between M/s Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shivamma & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that "if the claimants were not dependent on the income of the deceased, compensation under the head "Loss of dependency" cannot be granted.
At best in which circumstances, a nominal sum as compensation towards "loss of estate" can be granted by applying an appropriate multiplier.

It was further held that " where the claimants who are dependents of the deceased claims loss of dependency and where the claimants who are not the dependents of the deceased claim only loss to estate".
25.

In both the cases, by considering that the claimants are not the dependents of the deceased but only the legal representatives of the deceased, the Hon'ble High Court has awarded compensation under the head loss of estate but not under the head loss of dependency.

Further the loss of estate was calculated by taking the amount spent for personal living expense as 3/4th of the income and savings was taken as 1/4th and adopted multiplier which is applicable to the age group of the deceased.

26. Now if the Notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- out of which, if 3/4th is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased there remains Rs.4,125/- per month as the savings of deceased.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 56 to 60 years is '9'.

Hence, the loss of estate would be (Rs.4,125 x 9x12) = Rs.4,45,500/-.
27.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost his wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 lost their mother, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

28. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
29.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/- 2 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/- funeral expenses 3 Loss of spousal Rs.1,45,200/-
Shankarachary vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143280099/
7 consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium (Rs.48,400x3) 4 Loss of dependency Rs.4,45,500/-
Total Rs.6,27,000/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.6,27,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh Twenty Seven Thousand Only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
30.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2 nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

31. Hence, the respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 is liable to pay compensation to an extent of 50% and remaining 50%
compensation shall be paid by the respondent no.4 being the insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ND-6489.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,27,000/- + cost of Rs.3,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.II, III, IV.
The petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.6,30,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh Thirty Thousand only).
A Sum of Rs.6,27,000/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.3,13,500/- +
cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.IV.

The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.3,15,000/- (Rupees Three Lakh Fifteen Thousand only) with interest at 6%
within 2 months from the date of this award.

The Respondent No 4 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.3,13,500/- +
cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II & III.

The respondent no.4 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.3,15,000/-(Rupees Three Lakh Fifteen Thousand only) with interest at 6%
within 2 months from the date of this award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.3,30,000/-, Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.1,50,000/- each.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions time and again has observed that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof and the Tribunal has to independently decide the case based on the evidence placed on record.
But in the present case from the spot mahazar and from the IMV report it can be gathered that negligence was contributed by the driver of both the vehicles.
Hence,
considering the materials placed on record this court is of the opinion that the driver of the both vehicles have contributed negligence at the ratio of 50:50.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner no.2 is the married daughter and petitioner no.3 is the major son of the deceased.
Hence, the petitioners being the husband, married daughter and major son of the deceased are not the dependents of the deceased though they are the legal heirs of the deceased.

Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
